title: A failed quote refresh disables staleness detection, so the button stays enabled on an outdated summary and burns create attempts
claim: S14.8 blocks submit while `stale || !quote.ok`. But `stale` is defined with `!quoteFailed`, so as soon as a refresh fails (with a quote already on screen) staleness is switched off. The summary keeps the old shipping, discount and total, and the button stays enabled. The submit sends the new city or coupon with the old quoteHash, and the server answers QUOTE_CHANGED (409). checkout_create takes the per-IP (10/h) and per-email (5/h) throttles and a Turnstile verification before it reaches the price check (SQL:879-917), so each such attempt is spent. The QUOTE_CHANGED branch (lines 294-300) then does not clear quoteFailed or update quoteKey, so the failure banner also stays on top of a fresh quote.
quote: const stale = quote !== null && !quoteFailed && quoteKey !== currentKey
failure_scenario: A buyer with a physical cart picks Riyadh (quote OK). They switch to Jeddah and the debounced quote request drops (mobile network blip), so quoteFailed=true. The summary still shows Riyadh shipping and the button is enabled. The buyer presses «تأكيد الطلب», which sends cityKey=jeddah with the Riyadh quoteHash, and the server answers 409 QUOTE_CHANGED. One of the buyer's 5 hourly create attempts is gone, and the «تعذّر تحديث الأسعار» banner remains over the freshly returned quote.
suggested_fix: Compute stale as `quote !== null && quoteKey !== currentKey` (independent of quoteFailed) so submit stays blocked until a quote for the current inputs arrives. In the QUOTE_CHANGED branch also call setQuoteKey(currentKey) and setQuoteFailed(false).

title: A confirm press that was answered with a Turnstile failure is still 'pending', so a later Turnstile recovery submits the order without a new press
claim: awaitingToken is set on a press made before the token exists (line 233). It is cleared only when submit() later passes validation and reaches line 237. If Turnstile fires error-callback while waiting, useTurnstile sets failed=true and token=''. `waiting` becomes false, so the button is re-enabled with the normal label, and the note «تعذّر تحميل التحقق؛ حدّث الصفحة.» appears. awaitingToken stays true. src/lib/turnstile.ts:64-67 clears `failed` and sets a token on a later successful callback, so recovery is an anticipated path. The effect below then fires requestSubmit() on its own.
failure_scenario: The buyer presses «تأكيد الطلب» before the check finishes. Turnstile errors, and the page says to refresh. The buyer instead edits the address. Turnstile auto-retries and returns a token. The effect calls requestSubmit(), and the order (a 20-minute hold) is created from the current form state. No press followed the error message.
suggested_fix: Clear awaitingToken when turnstileFailed becomes true, for example `useEffect(() => { if (turnstileFailed) setAwaitingToken(false) }, [turnstileFailed])`, or also call setAwaitingToken(false) in the `turnstileFailed` branch at line 229.

title: City list failures and an empty city list are silent: the buyer of a physical cart gets a dead select and only «اختر مدينة التوصيل»
claim: fetchCities returns [] on a non-OK response (quote.ts:280) and the catch here also maps errors to []. It is called once on mount, with no retry and no state that distinguishes 'failed' from 'none served'. shipping_rates only exposes rows that are enabled and priced to anon, and D09 says an unpriced city is not served, so an empty list is a legitimate state too. In either case the physical branch renders a select containing only «اختر المدينة». The summary and the field error both say «اختر مدينة التوصيل.», which the buyer cannot satisfy.
failure_scenario: The REST call to /rest/v1/shipping_rates times out, or the owner has enabled no city yet. A buyer with a physical cart sees the city select with a single placeholder option. Pressing confirm shows «اختر مدينة التوصيل.» forever. Nothing says delivery is unavailable or that the list failed to load, and there is no retry.
suggested_fix: Keep a `citiesState` of 'loading' | 'failed' | 'loaded'. For 'failed' show an alert with a retry. For a loaded empty list show «لا نوصل إلى أي مدينة حاليًا» and disable submit.

title: Coupon input has no length cap; a code over 64 characters makes every quote fail and, after a reload, leaves checkout as a dead end
claim: The checkout function bounds couponCode at 64 characters (_shared/checkout.ts:46, and :66 for create). A longer value is refused at the schema step with 422 INVALID, so fetchQuote throws (quote.ts:229-231) and only the generic «تعذّر تحديث الأسعار؛ أعد المحاولة بعد لحظات.» appears. That message blames the connection. The name (120) and address (500) inputs in this form carry maxLength, but the coupon input does not. applyCoupon persists the value to sessionStorage, and the mount effect restores it (lines 117-121). On the next reload of /checkout the first quote fails with quote===null, so the page is replaced by the «أعد المحاولة» view (lines 421-430). That view has no coupon field and no link to /cart, and its retry re-sends the same bad code.
failure_scenario: A buyer pastes a 70-character string into «كود الخصم» and presses «تطبيق». The quote fails with a misleading network message. They reload the page. Checkout now shows only «تعذّر تحديث الأسعار» and «أعد المحاولة», and retrying never succeeds, because the saved coupon is re-sent every time. The only escape is finding the header cart link and clearing the coupon there.
suggested_fix: Add maxLength={64} to the coupon input in CheckoutForm (and CartView). In the quote-failed view render the coupon field or a link to /cart. When the function answers 422 for a quote, drop the stored coupon.

title: writeCart persists a whole-cart snapshot from React state, so a stale /cart tab silently deletes items added in another tab
claim: CartView computes every edit from the cart it loaded at mount, e.g. update(setQuantity(cart, ...)). CartProvider.update passes it straight to writeCart, which overwrites the localStorage key. Nothing re-reads storage before the write. CartProvider reads once on mount and has no `storage` listener. CartLink was given one (S14.11), which shows the design expects cross-tab changes.
failure_scenario: Tab A shows /cart with [book X]. In tab B the buyer adds product Y, so storage is [X, Y]. Back in tab A the header count reads 2 but the page lists only X. The buyer presses «+» on X, which writes [X×2] and drops Y. No message is shown, and Y is gone from every tab.
suggested_fix: Make edits read-modify-write: have `update` accept an updater function applied to readCart().cart just before writing. Also refresh CartProvider state on the window `storage` event, as CartLink does.

title: Cart quote failure tells the buyer to retry but offers no retry, and nothing retries
claim: When the quote request fails (network blip, HTTP 5xx, the quote throttle returning 429), CartView sets quoteFailed and shows «أعد المحاولة بعد لحظات». The effect at lines 103-127 depends only on ready, storedCart, city and coupon, so it never runs again on its own. There is no button and no timer. AUDIT-1 S14.3 fixed the same defect in CheckoutForm by adding an «أعد المحاولة» ActionButton wired to refreshQuote (CheckoutForm.tsx ~421-427). The cart page, which is the first page of the flow, did not get it.
quote:
{quoteFailed &&

تعذّر تحديث الأسعار؛ أعد المحاولة بعد لحظات.

}
failure_scenario: The buyer opens /cart with two lines and the first quote returns 500 or 429. quote stays null, so every line title and price renders «…», there are no totals and no checkout link. The alert says to retry after a moment, but no control exists and no timer fires. The buyer can recover only by reloading, or by changing a quantity, coupon or city to change the effect deps.
suggested_fix: Add an «أعد المحاولة» ActionButton beside the alert that re-runs the quote. Use a retry counter in the effect deps, or reuse the refreshQuote pattern from CheckoutForm. Alternatively retry once automatically after a few seconds.

title: Coupon field has no length bound; an over-long code makes every quote fail with a misleading message and survives reload
claim: The checkout function's quote schema is `couponCode: z.string().max(64)` (supabase/functions/_shared/checkout.ts:46) and the database code pattern is `^[A-Z0-9]{3,32}$`. The input has no maxLength. «تطبيق» stores the trimmed, upper-cased text in sessionStorage (COUPON_KEY), which is restored on mount. A 65+ character value gets HTTP 422 INVALID. fetchQuote throws on !reply.ok, so CartView shows the generic price-update failure instead of «كود الخصم غير صالح». The CheckoutForm coupon input has the same gap.
failure_scenario: The buyer pastes a 70-character string (a URL or a sentence) into «كود الخصم» and taps «تطبيق». Every quote now gets 422. The cart turns into the failed state (lines show «…», no totals, no checkout link) with a message that suggests a network problem. Reloading does not help because the coupon is restored from sessionStorage. Nothing points at the coupon field.
suggested_fix: Add maxLength={32} to the coupon inputs in the cart and in CheckoutForm, matching the DB pattern. Optionally map a 422 INVALID reply on quote to the COUPON_INVALID message when a coupon was sent.

title: Dedication inputs on different lines share one accessible name
claim: AUDIT-1 X3.11 gave the quantity, ± and «حذف» controls per-line names built from `name`. The dedication input inside the same line card is still labelled by the bare text «نص الإهداء», so every signed line exposes the same name. A screen-reader user moving through the form controls cannot tell which product a field belongs to.
failure_scenario: The cart holds two signed books. Tabbing through the controls, a screen-reader user hears «نص الإهداء» twice with no product name and cannot tell which book each field is for. This is the same problem X3.11 fixed for the other controls.
suggested_fix: Add `aria-label={`نص الإهداء: ${name}`}` to the input, or a visually-hidden `: {name}` inside the label as AddToCart does.

title: Cart is read once on mount and then written back whole, so another tab's additions are overwritten
claim: CartProvider reads localStorage once. update() then writes the full `next` cart built from that in-memory snapshot. CartLink listens to 'storage' and CART_EVENT, but CartProvider never re-syncs from other tabs. Any edit on /cart (quantity, «حذف», dedication) or /checkout overwrites the shared `anasaq:cart:v1` with the stale snapshot.
failure_scenario: Tab A shows /cart with one line. In tab B the buyer opens a product and adds a second item, which writes localStorage. Back in tab A the second item is not shown. The buyer taps «حذف» on the first line, and A writes a cart without the second item. The item added in B is silently lost, and the «السلة (n)» link in B drops to match.
suggested_fix: In CartProvider, listen to 'storage' (and CART_EVENT) and call setState(readCart()). Or re-read readCart() inside update() and apply the mutation to the fresh cart.

title: S06.8 fix leaves the partial-cap case: an add clamped by addLine still says «أُضيف إلى السلة»
claim: AUDIT-1 S06.8 was «confirms an add that addLine refused or capped». The fix compares cartCount before and after and only reports a refusal when nothing changed. addLine also caps a merged line at 20 (`Math.min(MAX_QUANTITY, l.quantity + quantity)`), so a partial add changes the count and passes this check. The note then claims success and gives only the whole-cart count.
failure_scenario: The cart holds 18 of a variant plus 4 items in other lines. The buyer sets the quantity to 5 and taps «أضف إلى السلة». The cart goes from 18 to 20, only 2 of the 5 are added, and the note says «أُضيف إلى السلة. في السلة الآن 24.». The buyer believes 5 were added and does not learn that the per-product maximum of 20 clipped the add.
suggested_fix: Compare the added amount with the requested one: `const added = cartCount(next) - cartCount(cart)`. If `added < quantity`, say that only `added` were added because the maximum is 20 per product. Keep the current message for added === 0.

title: Store grid paints unfilled cells solid aubergine when the product count is not a multiple of the column count
claim: `.grid` draws its 1px lines by giving the container `background: var(--aub)` with `gap: 1px; padding: 1px` and giving each card an opaque sand background. `repeat(auto-fit, …)` collapses only completely empty tracks, and an incomplete last row leaves empty cells in tracks that hold items in row 1. The container background shows through those cells as solid blocks. The scenes gallery handles the same case deliberately (its grid draws the weave behind an unfilled row). The store grid does not.
failure_scenario: At 1440px the list has 4 columns. With 5 published products, row 2 has one card and three empty cells rendered as a solid aubergine block roughly 900px wide. With 3 demo products at a 2-column width (about 640-900px), the third card sits next to one solid aubergine cell. The demo catalog's 3 products fill one row at 1440 and 360, so the visual pass did not show it.
suggested_fix: Draw the hairlines on the cards instead (border or box-shadow on `.card`, container background transparent). Or paint the weave behind the unfilled cells as in scenes.module.css.

title: Coupon field has no maxLength; a >64-char value makes every quote fail and the persisted value dead-ends /checkout
claim: The function caps couponCode at 64 (quoteSchema and createSchema in _shared/checkout.ts), and a 422 INVALID makes fetchQuote() throw, which the form treats as a generic quote failure. Neither coupon input (this one, and CartView.tsx:272) has maxLength. applyCoupon() also writes the value to sessionStorage under COUPON_KEY. On the next load of /checkout the saved coupon is restored before the first quote, so the request fails with quote === null. The S14.3 view shown then contains only the message and «أعد المحاولة», which repeats the same failing request. The coupon field is not rendered in that view, so the buyer cannot fix the cause.
failure_scenario: The buyer pastes a whole WhatsApp line containing a code (more than 64 chars) into the cart coupon box and presses «تطبيق». The cart quote fails with a generic alert. If a good quote was already on screen, the «المتابعة لإتمام الطلب» link is still shown. On /checkout the persisted coupon fails every quote, so the buyer sees only «تعذّر تحديث الأسعار» and a retry that always fails, with no coupon field to clear.
suggested_fix: Add maxLength={64} to both coupon inputs. Optionally drop a saved coupon when the quote fails with quote === null, or render the coupon field in the failure view.

verdict: split (verify first; fix only if real)
title: Hold and cancel results are still not conveyed: focus lands on a group named only by the order number
claim:
AUDIT-1 S14.5 is fixed by focusing the order box after create or cancel. The box is role="group" with aria-labelledby pointing at the order-number paragraph only. The hold text at line 399 is a plain

with no role. The cancel result at lines 390-392 is a role="status" paragraph that is mounted already filled in the same render that mounts the box. This is the pattern the same commit treats as missed by screen readers when it fixes X3.12 (AddToCart) and S13.5 (VideoTile) by keeping the region mounted. With focus on the group, the announcement is its name and role, not the paragraphs inside it.
failure_scenario: A screen-reader buyer confirms the order and hears "رقم الطلب: ABCDEFGH, مجموعة". They never hear that it is a 20-minute hold with no charge. After «إلغاء الطلب» they hear the same label, not «أُلغي الطلب.».
suggested_fix: Give the group aria-describedby pointing at the hold/closed paragraph ids (or fold the message into the labelledby text). Alternatively keep one always-mounted role="status" paragraph in the order box and only change its text.

title: A capped (partial) add is still confirmed as a full add
claim: S06.8 ("confirms an add that addLine refused or capped") is fixed only for the case where nothing changes. addLine clamps the merged quantity to 20, so adding 5 to a line already at 18 adds 2. cartCount(next) then differs from cartCount(cart), the refusal branch is skipped, and the status says «أُضيف إلى السلة. في السلة الآن N.» with N the total across all lines. The buyer is never told that only part of the request was added.
failure_scenario: The cart holds 18 of variant X. The buyer enters 5 and presses «أضف إلى السلة». Only 2 units are added (capped at 20), but the note reads «أُضيف إلى السلة. في السلة الآن 20.», so the buyer believes 5 more were added.
suggested_fix: Compare the requested quantity with the delta: `const added = cartCount(next) - cartCount(cart)`. If added < quantity, say that only `added` were added and that the maximum is 20 per product.

title: Cart page never re-reads storage, so an edit made on a stale cart tab overwrites items added in another tab
claim: CartProvider reads localStorage once on mount (line 30) and update() writes the whole cart built from that tab's in-memory state (line 36). Unlike CartLink.tsx it has no 'storage' or CART_EVENT listener. AddToCart on a product page in another tab does a read-modify-write of the same key. Any later quantity, dedication or delete edit on the stale /cart tab therefore replaces the stored cart with the stale lines, silently dropping items added elsewhere. The cart's quote is computed from the same stale state, so the missing item is not shown either. The server re-prices whatever lines it receives, so this is not a price error, but the buyer loses cart lines without a message.
failure_scenario: Tab A shows /cart with variant V1. In tab B the buyer opens a product page and presses «أضف إلى السلة» for V2; localStorage now holds [V1, V2]. Back in tab A the buyer presses + on V1: update(setQuantity(cart, V1, 2)) writes [V1 x2] built from tab A's state, so V2 disappears from storage and from the CartLink count, and checkout orders only V1.
suggested_fix: In CartProvider subscribe to window 'storage' (other tabs) and re-run readCart() into state, or make update() read the stored cart and apply the mutation to it (mutations are pure functions over CartV1) instead of writing the in-memory copy.

title: Removing a cart line deletes the focused button; focus is lost and the removal is not announced
claim: «حذف» removes the whole <li>, including the button that has focus, and «إزالة غير المتاح» (line 242) does the same for several lines. Focus goes to <body>. The always-mounted total status announces a new total only after the ~300 ms requote, and when the last line goes the whole view is replaced by «سلتك فارغة.» (a subtree that was never in a live region), so that case announces nothing.
failure_scenario: A keyboard user removes the first of four lines with Enter. Focus resets to the top of the document and they must Tab back through the header and the earlier lines. Removing the only line gives no spoken result at all.
suggested_fix: After a removal, move focus to the next line's first control (or the list/summary heading, tabIndex -1) and put «حُذف المنتج» or «سلتك فارغة.» in the existing always-mounted role=status element.

title: Field errors sit in non-live spans, so pressing Enter in the field that is already focused announces nothing
claim: When validation fails, submit() sets the errors and calls focus() on the first invalid field. If that field already has focus, focus() is a no-op and the only change is text in a plain <span> plus new aria-invalid/aria-describedby attributes; none of these is announced by screen readers. The contact form has the same shape (ContactForm.tsx:144, an always-mounted span with no role or aria-live). AUDIT-1 X3.4 judged the pattern correct because focus normally moves, which holds only when the user submits from the button or another field.
failure_scenario: On /checkout a screen-reader user types a malformed email and presses Enter in that same field. The «أدخل بريدًا إلكترونيًا صحيحًا.» text appears but focus does not move and no live region fires, so nothing is spoken and the form seems to do nothing. The same happens for the name field, and on /contact for the name and email fields.
suggested_fix: Give the error element role="alert" (or render the first error into the existing always-mounted status region) so it is announced whether or not focus moves.

title: A coupon over 64 characters makes every quote fail; after a reload checkout shows only a retry button that can never succeed
claim: Neither coupon input has a `maxLength` (CartView.tsx:272 and CheckoutForm.tsx:484), while the function's quote and create schemas cap `couponCode` at 64 (checkout.ts:46, :66). An over-long code gets 422 INVALID for the whole quote. `fetchQuote` throws with that message, and both callers discard it and show 'تعذّر تحديث الأسعار؛ أعد المحاولة بعد لحظات.' The code is stored in sessionStorage (COUPON_KEY) and restored on load. In CheckoutForm, with `quote === null` the only output is the retry screen below, which has no coupon input, so retrying resends the same code (S14.3's retry fix does not help here). The way out is to go to /cart and clear the code there. Same class, smaller: the email input has no `maxLength` against `.max(254)` and the phone input none against `.max(64)`, and the function's default English zod message is mapped verbatim under the field (line 314).
failure_scenario: Buyer pastes a 70-character string into «كود الخصم» on /cart or /checkout and presses «تطبيق». The quote returns 422 and the page says prices could not be refreshed, try again. The buyer reloads /checkout: the stored code is restored, the quote fails again with no quote to render, and the page shows only «تعذّر تحديث الأسعار» and «أعد المحاولة». No coupon field is available and retrying never works.
suggested_fix: Add `maxLength={32}` to both coupon inputs (the DB code cap). In CheckoutForm, render the coupon field (or a «إزالة الكود» action) in the failed-quote state, or drop a stored coupon when a quote with it fails with 422. Add `maxLength={254}` to email.
